concepts.name: accretion_disk
concepts.definition: Rotating disk of gas and dust spiraling onto a central body, losing angular momentum and radiating as it slowly falls inward.

concepts.name: chandrasekhar_limit
concepts.definition: Maximum mass (~1.4 solar masses) of a stable white dwarf, above which electron degeneracy pressure cannot resist gravitational collapse.

concepts.name: cosmic_microwave_background
concepts.definition: Relic blackbody microwave radiation filling all space, released ~380,000 years after the Big Bang when atoms formed and the universe became transparent.

concepts.name: gravitational_lensing
concepts.definition: Bending of light from a distant source by the curved spacetime of a massive foreground body, distorting and magnifying its image.

concepts.name: hertzsprung_russell_diagram
concepts.definition: Scatter plot of stellar luminosity versus temperature that reveals the main sequence and groupings used to study stellar evolution.

concepts.name: orbital_resonance
concepts.definition: Periodic mutual gravitational influence between orbiting bodies whose orbital periods form a ratio of small integers.

concepts.name: redshift
concepts.definition: Shift of an astronomical object's spectrum toward longer wavelengths from relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion of space.

concepts.name: stellar_nucleosynthesis
concepts.definition: Creation of chemical elements by nuclear fusion within stars, building heavier nuclei from lighter ones as stars evolve.

concepts.name: stellar_parallax
concepts.definition: Apparent shift of a nearby star against distant background as Earth orbits the Sun, used to triangulate stellar distances.

concepts.name: allometry
concepts.definition: Study of how organismal traits scale with body size, often as a power law Y = aM^b across morphology, physiology, and ecology.

concepts.name: circadian_rhythm
concepts.definition: Endogenous biological oscillation with a period near 24 hours that is entrained by environmental cues such as light.

concepts.name: enzyme_catalysis
concepts.definition: Acceleration of a biochemical reaction by an enzyme that binds substrate at its active site and lowers the activation barrier.

concepts.name: mimicry
concepts.definition: Evolved resemblance of one organism to another or to its surroundings, often deceiving predators to gain protection.

concepts.name: morphogenesis
concepts.definition: Biological process by which a cell, tissue, or organism develops its shape via organized cell division, migration, and adhesion.

concepts.name: negative_feedback_inhibition
concepts.definition: Regulatory mechanism where a pathway's end product inhibits an earlier enzyme, preventing overproduction and maintaining homeostasis.

concepts.name: phenotypic_plasticity
concepts.definition: Ability of a single genotype to produce multiple phenotypes in response to differing environmental conditions.

concepts.name: signal_transduction
concepts.definition: Transmission of a molecular signal from a cell's exterior to interior via a cascade of reactions producing a cellular response.

concepts.name: symbiosis
concepts.definition: Close, long-term biological interaction between two different species, spanning mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism.

concepts.name: activation_energy
concepts.definition: The minimum energy barrier reactants must overcome to form products; higher activation energy yields slower reaction rates (Arrhenius).

concepts.name: buffer_solution
concepts.definition: A weak acid-base conjugate pair that resists pH change on adding small amounts of acid or base via a chemical equilibrium.

concepts.name: chelation
concepts.definition: Bonding of a metal ion by a polydentate ligand forming multiple coordinate bonds and a ring, yielding an unusually stable metal complex.

concepts.name: distillation
concepts.definition: Separating components of a liquid mixture by selective boiling and condensation, exploiting differences in their boiling points.

concepts.name: electrolysis
concepts.definition: Using direct electric current to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction, decomposing an ionic compound into elements at the electrodes.

concepts.name: electronegativity
concepts.definition: A measure of an atom's tendency to attract a shared bonding electron pair; differences between atoms set bond polarity and ionic character.

concepts.name: hydrogen_bonding
concepts.definition: An attractive interaction between a hydrogen bonded to an electronegative donor (N, O, F) and a lone pair on another electronegative atom.

concepts.name: polymerization
concepts.definition: A reaction joining many monomer molecules into long-chain or networked polymers built from repeating units.

concepts.name: redox_reaction
concepts.definition: A reaction in which electrons transfer between species, changing oxidation states; oxidation (electron loss) and reduction (electron gain) occur together.

concepts.name: b_tree
concepts.definition: Self-balancing multi-way search tree keeping sorted keys in wide nodes for logarithmic disk-friendly search, insertion, and deletion.

concepts.name: garbage_collection
concepts.definition: Automatic memory management that reclaims heap storage no longer referenced by a program, preventing leaks without manual deallocation.

concepts.name: hash_table
concepts.definition: Associative array mapping keys to values by using a hash function to index an array of buckets for near constant-time lookup.

concepts.name: lru_cache
concepts.definition: Cache eviction policy that discards the least recently used item when full, exploiting temporal locality of access.

concepts.name: lsm_tree
concepts.definition: Write-optimized structure buffering updates in memory then batching them down append-only disk tiers via merge, easing high insert volume.

concepts.name: memoization
concepts.definition: Optimization that caches results of expensive function calls and returns the stored result for repeated identical inputs.

concepts.name: mvcc
concepts.definition: Concurrency control keeping multiple data versions so readers see a consistent snapshot without blocking writers, avoiding locks.

concepts.name: skip_list
concepts.definition: Probabilistic ordered structure layering linked lists with randomized express lanes to give average logarithmic search, insert, and delete.

concepts.name: trie
concepts.definition: Prefix tree storing strings along paths where edges are characters, letting shared prefixes share nodes for fast string lookup.

concepts.name: adaptive_control
concepts.definition: Control method that adjusts controller parameters online via real-time parameter estimation to handle uncertain or time-varying plant dynamics.

concepts.name: bang_bang_control
concepts.definition: Feedback controller that switches abruptly between extreme input values, optimal for many time-optimal problems with bounded actuation.

concepts.name: feedforward_control
concepts.definition: Proactive control that measures disturbances and applies a compensating input to counteract them before they affect the output, using a process model.

concepts.name: gain_scheduling
concepts.definition: Control of nonlinear systems via a family of linear controllers selected by scheduling variables that identify the current operating region.

concepts.name: h_infinity_control
concepts.definition: Robust control synthesis that minimizes the worst-case H-infinity norm (peak gain over frequency) to guarantee stability and performance under uncertainty.

concepts.name: linear_quadratic_regulator
concepts.definition: Optimal state-feedback law that minimizes a quadratic cost trading off state error against control effort, solved via the algebraic Riccati equation.

concepts.name: pole_placement
concepts.definition: State-feedback design that computes a gain matrix to assign closed-loop poles (eigenvalues) to desired locations, requiring system controllability.

concepts.name: root_locus
concepts.definition: Graphical method tracing how closed-loop poles move in the s-plane as a feedback gain varies from zero to infinity, used as a stability criterion.

concepts.name: sliding_mode_control
concepts.definition: Nonlinear control applying a discontinuous switching law to force trajectories onto a sliding surface, giving insensitivity to matched disturbances.

concepts.name: cryptographic_hash_function
concepts.definition: A deterministic one-way function mapping arbitrary input to a fixed-length digest, with collision resistance and an avalanche effect.

concepts.name: diffie_hellman_key_exchange
concepts.definition: A protocol letting two parties jointly derive a shared secret key over a public channel, with security resting on the hardness of discrete logarithms.

concepts.name: digital_signature
concepts.definition: A cryptographic scheme using asymmetric keys to verify the authenticity and integrity of a message and provide non-repudiation of the signer.

concepts.name: elliptic_curve_cryptography
concepts.definition: Public-key cryptography based on the algebraic structure of elliptic curves over finite fields, giving equivalent security with smaller keys.

concepts.name: homomorphic_encryption
concepts.definition: Encryption permitting computation on ciphertexts so that decrypting the result matches operations performed on the underlying plaintext.

concepts.name: oblivious_transfer
concepts.definition: A protocol where a sender transfers one of several items to a receiver while remaining oblivious to which item, if any, was received.

concepts.name: public_key_infrastructure
concepts.definition: A framework of certificates and authorities that binds public keys to identities, enabling trusted distribution and verification of keys.

concepts.name: ring_signature
concepts.definition: A digital signature any member of a set can produce, proving someone in the group signed while hiding which signer's key was used.

concepts.name: rsa_cryptosystem
concepts.definition: A public-key cryptosystem using a paired public and private key whose security rests on the difficulty of factoring the product of two large primes.

concepts.name: byzantine_fault_tolerance
concepts.definition: Property letting a network reach consensus despite up to one-third of nodes failing arbitrarily or behaving maliciously.

concepts.name: crdt
concepts.definition: Replicated data type whose mathematically constrained operations let replicas update independently yet deterministically converge to one state.

concepts.name: lamport_timestamp
concepts.definition: Logical clock assigning monotonically increasing counters to events so the happened-before relation yields a consistent event order.

concepts.name: leader_election
concepts.definition: Process by which distributed nodes designate exactly one coordinator to organize a shared task, satisfying safety and liveness.

concepts.name: mapreduce
concepts.definition: Programming model processing large datasets in parallel across a cluster via a map phase that transforms and a reduce phase that aggregates.

concepts.name: paxos
concepts.definition: Consensus protocol family where proposers, acceptors, and learners agree on a single value despite node failures and message delays.

concepts.name: raft
concepts.definition: Understandable consensus algorithm where an elected leader replicates an ordered log to followers, tolerating a minority of node failures.

concepts.name: two_phase_commit
concepts.definition: Atomic commitment protocol where a coordinator runs a prepare-vote phase then a commit-or-abort phase across all participants.

concepts.name: vector_clock
concepts.definition: Array of per-node counters exchanged between processes to establish causal partial ordering of events and detect concurrency.

concepts.name: competitive_exclusion
concepts.definition: Gause's principle that two species competing for the same limiting resource cannot coexist; one outcompetes or forces a niche shift.

concepts.name: ecological_resilience
concepts.definition: The capacity of an ecosystem to absorb disturbance and reorganize while retaining essentially the same function, structure, and feedbacks.

concepts.name: insular_biogeography
concepts.definition: Theory that island species richness reaches equilibrium set by immigration and extinction rates, scaling with island area and isolation.

concepts.name: metapopulation
concepts.definition: A set of spatially separated local populations of one species linked by migration, with balance between local extinction and recolonization.

concepts.name: mutualism
concepts.definition: An ecological interaction between species in which each partner gains a net benefit, often becoming interdependent for survival.

concepts.name: niche_partitioning
concepts.definition: Coexisting species divide resources by habitat, food, or time so that direct competition is reduced and each can persist.

concepts.name: nutrient_cycling
concepts.definition: The biogeochemical movement and reuse of elements like carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus through organisms and the environment in a loop.

concepts.name: predator_prey_dynamics
concepts.definition: Coupled oscillations of predator and prey populations described by the Lotka-Volterra equations, with predators lagging prey peaks.

concepts.name: primary_production
concepts.definition: The synthesis of organic biomass from CO2 by autotrophs via photosynthesis or chemosynthesis, forming the energetic base of food webs.

concepts.name: adverse_selection
concepts.definition: Asymmetric information lets the informed party exploit hidden attributes, degrading market quality as good types exit (e.g. lemons, insurance).

concepts.name: creative_destruction
concepts.definition: Schumpeter's process by which innovation continually destroys old industries and creates new ones, driving the dynamic evolution of capitalism.

concepts.name: externality
concepts.definition: A cost or benefit imposed on an uninvolved third party not reflected in market prices, causing social and private costs to diverge.

concepts.name: moral_hazard
concepts.definition: Agents take on more risk or shirk effort because a counterparty bears the cost, arising under hidden actions and information asymmetry.

concepts.name: network_effect
concepts.definition: A product or service gains value as more users adopt it, the demand-side counterpart of economies of scale that can raise entry barriers.

concepts.name: price_elasticity_of_demand
concepts.definition: Measure of the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change, as percentage change in quantity over percentage change in price.

concepts.name: principal_agent_problem
concepts.definition: Conflict when a principal delegates to an agent with misaligned incentives and information asymmetry, yielding outcomes worse than the principal wants.

concepts.name: public_good
concepts.definition: A good that is non-excludable and non-rivalrous, so markets under-provide it due to the free-rider problem.

concepts.name: tragedy_of_the_commons
concepts.definition: Individuals overuse a shared rivalrous, non-excludable resource because costs are collective, leading to depletion against the common interest.

concepts.name: attack_rate
concepts.definition: The proportion of an at-risk population that contracts a disease during a specified interval, used in outbreak investigation.

concepts.name: basic_reproduction_number
concepts.definition: R0, the expected number of secondary cases generated by one infectious case in a fully susceptible population; R0>1 lets an epidemic grow.

concepts.name: case_fatality_rate
concepts.definition: The proportion of people diagnosed with a disease who die from it, used as a measure of disease severity.

concepts.name: confounding
concepts.definition: Distortion of an exposure-outcome association by a third variable linked to both but not on the causal pathway, biasing causal inference.

concepts.name: contact_tracing
concepts.definition: Public-health process of identifying and following up people exposed to an infected case to break chains of transmission.

concepts.name: epidemic_curve
concepts.definition: A chart of case counts by date of symptom onset, used to visualize an outbreak's magnitude, trend, and likely mode of transmission.

concepts.name: herd_immunity
concepts.definition: Indirect protection from an infectious disease that arises once a large fraction of a population is immune, suppressing sustained transmission.

concepts.name: incidence_rate
concepts.definition: The rate at which new cases of a disease arise in an at-risk population over a time period, with person-time as the denominator.

concepts.name: sir_compartmental_model
concepts.definition: Compartmental model dividing a population into susceptible, infected, and recovered classes to predict infectious-disease dynamics over time.

concepts.name: dominant_strategy
concepts.definition: A strategy that yields a player a higher payoff than any alternative regardless of what the other players choose.

concepts.name: evolutionarily_stable_strategy
concepts.definition: A strategy that, once adopted by a population, cannot be invaded by any initially rare alternative; a Nash equilibrium refinement.

concepts.name: minimax_theorem
concepts.definition: Von Neumann's result that every finite two-person zero-sum game has optimal mixed strategies guaranteeing a value via worst-case optimization.

concepts.name: mixed_strategy
concepts.definition: A probability distribution over pure strategies by which a player randomizes their action rather than committing to one move.

concepts.name: nash_equilibrium
concepts.definition: A strategy profile where no player can improve their payoff by unilaterally changing strategy, given the others' fixed choices.

concepts.name: prisoners_dilemma
concepts.definition: Two rational agents each defect for individual gain even though mutual cooperation yields a higher payoff for both.

concepts.name: shapley_value
concepts.definition: Cooperative-game solution fairly distributing total gains by averaging each player's marginal contribution over all orderings of coalitions.

concepts.name: subgame_perfect_equilibrium
concepts.definition: A Nash equilibrium refinement for sequential games requiring equilibrium play in every subgame, eliminating non-credible threats via backward induction.

concepts.name: tit_for_tat
concepts.definition: Iterated-game strategy that cooperates first then mirrors the opponent's previous move, rewarding cooperation and punishing defection.

concepts.name: alternative_splicing
concepts.definition: Process where exons of a single gene are joined in different combinations, yielding multiple distinct mRNAs and proteins.

concepts.name: crispr
concepts.definition: Bacterial adaptive-immunity system repurposed for gene editing, using guide RNA to direct a Cas nuclease to cut DNA at a targeted sequence.

concepts.name: dna_methylation
concepts.definition: Epigenetic addition of a methyl group to cytosine that silences or modulates gene expression without altering the DNA sequence.

concepts.name: genetic_drift
concepts.definition: Random change in allele frequencies from generation to generation due to sampling error, most pronounced in small populations.

concepts.name: genetic_linkage
concepts.definition: Tendency of DNA sequences close together on a chromosome to be inherited together because recombination rarely separates them.

concepts.name: genetic_recombination
concepts.definition: Exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes during meiosis, producing new allele combinations in offspring.

concepts.name: genomic_imprinting
concepts.definition: Epigenetic phenomenon where a gene is expressed from only one parental allele, determined by the parent of origin.

concepts.name: hardy_weinberg_equilibrium
concepts.definition: Principle that allele and genotype frequencies stay constant across generations absent disturbing forces like selection, drift, or migration.

concepts.name: transcription_factor_regulation
concepts.definition: Control of gene expression by regulatory proteins that bind specific DNA sequences to activate or repress RNA polymerase recruitment.

concepts.name: geomagnetic_reversal
concepts.definition: Change in Earth's magnetic field in which magnetic north and south poles switch places, driven by the core dynamo at irregular times.

concepts.name: isostasy
concepts.definition: Gravitational equilibrium in which Earth's crust floats on the denser mantle at an elevation set by its thickness and density.

concepts.name: mantle_convection
concepts.definition: Slow creep of Earth's solid mantle that carries interior heat to the surface, with hot material rising and cool material sinking.

concepts.name: milankovitch_cycles
concepts.definition: Cyclic changes in Earth's orbital eccentricity, axial tilt, and precession that vary solar insolation and pace ice ages.

concepts.name: plate_tectonics
concepts.definition: Theory that Earth's lithosphere is divided into rigid plates that move and interact, driving earthquakes, volcanism, and mountain building.

concepts.name: radiometric_dating
concepts.definition: Dating materials by measuring radioactive isotope decay, using parent-to-daughter ratios and known half-lives to find absolute ages.

concepts.name: rock_cycle
concepts.definition: Geologic concept describing how igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks transform into one another over time via heat, pressure, and erosion.

concepts.name: seismic_tomography
concepts.definition: Imaging technique using seismic waves to reconstruct 2D/3D models of Earth's interior from variations in wave speed.

concepts.name: thermohaline_circulation
concepts.definition: Large-scale ocean circulation driven by density gradients from temperature and salinity, transporting heat and matter globally.

concepts.name: affinity_maturation
concepts.definition: Progressive increase in average antibody affinity over an immune response via somatic mutation and selective expansion of high-affinity B-cell clones.

concepts.name: central_tolerance
concepts.definition: Elimination via apoptosis of developing self-reactive T or B lymphocytes in the thymus or bone marrow to prevent autoimmunity.

concepts.name: class_switch_recombination
concepts.definition: B cells rearrange immunoglobulin heavy-chain constant genes to switch antibody class while keeping antigen specificity, altering effector function.

concepts.name: clonal_selection
concepts.definition: Antigen activates only the lymphocyte bearing a matching receptor, driving its proliferation into identical effector clones of that specificity.

concepts.name: complement_cascade
concepts.definition: Enzymatic serum-protein cascade where sequential zymogen cleavage amplifies an immune response, opsonizing pathogens and forming lytic pores.

concepts.name: cytokine_signaling
concepts.definition: Small secreted proteins bind cell-surface receptors to relay autocrine, paracrine and endocrine signals that coordinate immunity and inflammation.

concepts.name: mhc_antigen_presentation
concepts.definition: Display of processed peptide fragments on MHC molecules at the cell surface so T-cell receptors can recognize self versus non-self.

concepts.name: pattern_recognition_receptors
concepts.definition: Germline-encoded innate sensors that detect conserved pathogen- or damage-associated molecular patterns to trigger immune responses.

concepts.name: somatic_hypermutation
concepts.definition: AID-driven high-rate point mutation of immunoglobulin variable regions in germinal-center B cells, diversifying antibodies for affinity maturation.

concepts.name: arithmetic_coding
concepts.definition: Entropy coding that maps a whole message to a single fractional number in [0,1) by recursively partitioning intervals by symbol probability.

concepts.name: differential_entropy
concepts.definition: The continuous analog of Shannon entropy for absolutely continuous distributions, measuring uncertainty of a continuous random variable.

concepts.name: fano_inequality
concepts.definition: An inequality bounding the conditional entropy of a variable in terms of the error probability when estimating it, used in converse proofs.

concepts.name: hamming_distance
concepts.definition: The number of positions at which two equal-length strings differ, quantifying substitutions and underpinning error-detecting codes.

concepts.name: huffman_coding
concepts.definition: An algorithm building an optimal prefix code for lossless compression, assigning shorter codewords to more frequent source symbols.

concepts.name: kolmogorov_complexity
concepts.definition: The length of the shortest program that outputs a given string, measuring the information content of an individual object.

concepts.name: kullback_leibler_divergence
concepts.definition: A non-symmetric measure of the difference between two probability distributions, zero only when the distributions are identical.

concepts.name: slepian_wolf_coding
concepts.definition: A result in distributed source coding showing separated correlated sources can be compressed jointly down to their joint entropy.

concepts.name: typical_set
concepts.definition: The set of sequences whose probability is near two to the negative entropy of the source, carrying nearly all probability by the AEP.

concepts.name: batch_normalization
concepts.definition: Normalizes layer inputs over a mini-batch to zero mean and unit variance, then rescales and shifts, stabilizing and speeding training.

concepts.name: beam_search
concepts.definition: Decoding that keeps the k most probable partial sequences at each step, exploring multiple hypotheses to find higher-quality outputs than greedy.

concepts.name: data_augmentation
concepts.definition: Expands a dataset by applying label-preserving random transformations to existing samples, teaching invariance and improving generalization.

concepts.name: early_stopping
concepts.definition: Halts iterative training once validation performance stops improving, preventing the model from memorizing noise and overfitting.

concepts.name: ensemble_learning
concepts.definition: Combines predictions of multiple models, by averaging or voting, to reduce variance and improve accuracy beyond any single model.

concepts.name: label_smoothing
concepts.definition: Replaces hard one-hot targets with softened distributions mixing in uniform mass, penalizing overconfident predictions to improve generalization.

concepts.name: layer_normalization
concepts.definition: Normalizes activations across features within each data point, then scales and shifts, stabilizing training in sequential models and transformers.

concepts.name: transfer_learning
concepts.definition: Reuses knowledge from a model pretrained on one task to boost performance on a related task, often via fine-tuning, reducing data and compute needs.

concepts.name: weight_decay
concepts.definition: Regularization adding a penalty proportional to squared weight magnitude to the loss, shrinking parameters to discourage overfitting (L2 regularization).

concepts.name: dislocation_creep
concepts.definition: Time-dependent deformation under constant stress from thermally activated movement of dislocations by glide and climb.

concepts.name: grain_boundary_strengthening
concepts.definition: Hall-Petch strengthening where smaller grains give more boundaries that impede dislocations, raising yield strength.

concepts.name: ostwald_ripening
concepts.definition: Coarsening where smaller particles dissolve and redeposit onto larger ones, driven by reduction of interfacial energy.

concepts.name: piezoelectricity
concepts.definition: Certain non-centrosymmetric crystals generate electric charge under mechanical stress and deform under an applied electric field.

concepts.name: precipitation_hardening
concepts.definition: Heat treatment forming fine second-phase precipitates that impede dislocation motion, increasing alloy yield strength via aging.

concepts.name: shape_memory_effect
concepts.definition: Alloys recover a remembered shape after deformation via a reversible martensite-to-austenite phase transformation on heating.

concepts.name: sintering
concepts.definition: Heat-driven densification consolidating porous powder compacts into a denser solid via atomic diffusion and pore elimination.

concepts.name: spinodal_decomposition
concepts.definition: A single phase spontaneously separates into two phases by uphill diffusion without nucleation, forming a modulated structure.

concepts.name: work_hardening
concepts.definition: Strain hardening where plastic deformation multiplies and entangles dislocations, raising the stress needed for further flow.

concepts.name: dynamic_programming
concepts.definition: Optimization method that solves a complex problem by breaking it into overlapping subproblems and reusing their stored solutions.

concepts.name: fourier_transform
concepts.definition: Integral transform that decomposes a function into the frequencies present in it, mapping a signal from time to frequency domain.

concepts.name: gram_schmidt_process
concepts.definition: Algorithm that constructs an orthonormal basis from a set of linearly independent vectors by sequential orthogonalization and normalization.

concepts.name: lagrange_multipliers
concepts.definition: Method for finding local extrema of a function subject to equality constraints by introducing auxiliary multiplier variables.

concepts.name: linear_programming
concepts.definition: Optimization of a linear objective function subject to linear equality and inequality constraints over a convex polytope feasible region.

concepts.name: monte_carlo_integration
concepts.definition: Numerical integration technique that approximates an integral by averaging the integrand over randomly sampled points.

concepts.name: newtons_method
concepts.definition: Root-finding algorithm that produces successively better approximations to the zeros of a function using its derivative and tangent-line steps.

concepts.name: singular_value_decomposition
concepts.definition: Factorization of any matrix into a rotation, scaling, and rotation, exposing singular values; used for low-rank approximation and dimension reduction.

concepts.name: taylor_series
concepts.definition: Representation of a function as an infinite sum of terms built from its derivatives at one point, giving polynomial approximations near that point.

concepts.name: central_pattern_generator
concepts.definition: Neuronal network of excitatory and inhibitory neurons producing rhythmic motor output without sensory feedback, driving locomotion and breathing.

concepts.name: dendritic_computation
concepts.definition: Local linear and nonlinear integration of synaptic inputs within neuronal dendrites, letting single neurons perform elementary computations.

concepts.name: gamma_oscillations
concepts.definition: Rhythmic 30-90 Hz neural synchrony arising from excitatory-inhibitory interactions, linked to attention, perception and feature binding.

concepts.name: grid_cells
concepts.definition: Entorhinal neurons firing at vertices of a triangular lattice tiling space, providing a metric coordinate system for navigation.

concepts.name: long_term_potentiation
concepts.definition: Persistent activity-dependent strengthening of synaptic transmission following repeated stimulation; a core cellular substrate of learning and memory.

concepts.name: place_cells
concepts.definition: Hippocampal pyramidal neurons that fire selectively when an animal is in a particular location, forming a cognitive map of space.

concepts.name: population_coding
concepts.definition: Neural strategy in which information is represented by the joint activity pattern across many neurons rather than any single cell.

concepts.name: spike_timing_dependent_plasticity
concepts.definition: Synaptic change whose sign and size depend on the precise relative timing of pre- and postsynaptic spikes; a temporally asymmetric Hebbian rule.

concepts.name: synaptic_scaling
concepts.definition: Homeostatic plasticity that multiplicatively adjusts all of a neuron's synaptic strengths to stabilize firing while preserving relative weights.

concepts.name: assignment_problem
concepts.definition: Combinatorial problem of matching n tasks to n agents one-to-one at minimum total cost, solvable in polynomial time by the Hungarian method.

concepts.name: bin_packing
concepts.definition: Combinatorial problem of packing items of given sizes into the fewest fixed-capacity bins without exceeding capacity; NP-hard, solved via approximation.

concepts.name: critical_path_method
concepts.definition: Project scheduling technique finding the longest dependent task sequence that determines minimum project duration and the tasks with zero slack.

concepts.name: economic_order_quantity
concepts.definition: Inventory formula giving the order size that minimizes total holding plus ordering costs by balancing those two inversely related costs.

concepts.name: newsvendor_model
concepts.definition: Single-period inventory model choosing an order quantity that maximizes expected profit under uncertain demand, trading off overstock and understock.

concepts.name: queueing_theory
concepts.definition: Mathematical study of waiting lines that predicts queue lengths and waiting times to balance service cost against delay in service systems.

concepts.name: simplex_method
concepts.definition: Iterative linear programming algorithm moving between adjacent vertices of the feasible polytope in an improving direction until the optimum is reached.

concepts.name: traveling_salesman_problem
concepts.definition: Classic NP-hard problem of finding the shortest route visiting each of a set of cities exactly once and returning to the starting city.

concepts.name: vehicle_routing_problem
concepts.definition: Combinatorial optimization problem designing minimum-cost routes for a fleet of capacity-limited vehicles serving customers from a depot.

concepts.name: branch_and_bound
concepts.definition: Method for discrete optimization that enumerates candidate solutions as a tree, using bounds to prune branches that cannot beat the best found.

concepts.name: conjugate_gradient_method
concepts.definition: Iterative method solving positive-definite linear systems and energy minimization by stepping along mutually conjugate directions for fast convergence.

concepts.name: cutting_plane_method
concepts.definition: Iterative method refining a feasible set with valid linear inequalities (cuts) to exclude fractional points, used to solve integer and convex programs.

concepts.name: interior_point_method
concepts.definition: Algorithm solving constrained convex programs by following a central path through the interior of the feasible region guided by barrier functions.

concepts.name: line_search
concepts.definition: Iterative strategy that picks a descent direction then a step size along it satisfying acceptance conditions to ensure convergence to a stationary point.

concepts.name: proximal_gradient_method
concepts.definition: First-order splitting algorithm minimizing a sum of a smooth and a nonsmooth convex function by alternating a gradient step with a proximal operator.

concepts.name: subgradient_method
concepts.definition: Iterative algorithm minimizing nondifferentiable convex functions by stepping along a subgradient, generalizing gradient descent to nonsmooth objectives.

concepts.name: trust_region_method
concepts.definition: Iterative method minimizing a model approximating the objective within a region whose radius expands or contracts based on approximation fit quality.

concepts.name: bose_einstein_condensation
concepts.definition: A state of matter where bosons cooled near absolute zero collectively occupy the lowest quantum state, making quantum effects macroscopic.

concepts.name: brownian_motion
concepts.definition: Random motion of particles suspended in a fluid caused by collisions with fast-moving molecules, modeled as a random walk.

concepts.name: dimensional_analysis
concepts.definition: Buckingham pi method rewriting a relation among n variables with k dimensions as n-k dimensionless groups, reducing variables.

concepts.name: doppler_effect
concepts.definition: The change in observed wave frequency or period due to relative motion between a wave source and an observer.

concepts.name: noethers_theorem
concepts.definition: Every continuous symmetry of a physical system's action corresponds to a conserved quantity, linking invariance to conservation laws.

concepts.name: quantum_tunneling
concepts.definition: A quantum effect where a particle passes through a potential energy barrier it classically lacks the energy to surmount.

concepts.name: stimulated_emission
concepts.definition: An incoming photon induces an excited atom to emit a second coherent photon in the same mode, amplifying light as in lasers.

concepts.name: superconductivity
concepts.definition: Below a critical temperature certain materials exhibit zero electrical resistance and expel magnetic fields (Meissner effect).

concepts.name: total_internal_reflection
concepts.definition: Light in a denser medium hitting a boundary above the critical angle is fully reflected back rather than refracted.

concepts.name: artificial_potential_field
concepts.definition: Reactive path planning where the goal exerts an attractive force and obstacles exert repulsive forces, guiding the robot along the resulting gradient.

concepts.name: forward_kinematics
concepts.definition: Computing the pose of a robot's end-effector from given joint variables by chaining link transformations, often via Denavit-Hartenberg parameters.

concepts.name: impedance_control
concepts.definition: Interaction control that regulates the dynamic relation between end-effector motion and contact force, imposing a desired mass-spring-damper response.

concepts.name: inverse_kinematics
concepts.definition: Computing the joint parameters of a kinematic chain needed to place its end-effector at a desired position and orientation.

concepts.name: occupancy_grid_mapping
concepts.definition: Probabilistic technique representing an environment as a grid of cells, each holding the probability of being occupied, built from noisy sensor data.

concepts.name: probabilistic_roadmap
concepts.definition: Sampling-based motion planner that builds a graph of collision-free configurations, then queries it for paths between start and goal poses.

concepts.name: rapidly_exploring_random_tree
concepts.definition: Sampling-based motion planner that grows a space-filling tree by drawing random samples and extending toward them to search high-dimensional spaces.

concepts.name: simultaneous_localization_and_mapping
concepts.definition: Process by which a robot builds or updates a map of an unknown environment while concurrently estimating its own pose within that map.

concepts.name: visual_servoing
concepts.definition: Vision-based robot control that uses features extracted from camera images as feedback to drive the robot's motion toward a target configuration.

concepts.name: adaptive_filtering
concepts.definition: Filter whose coefficients are iteratively adjusted by an optimization rule (e.g. LMS) to minimize error between output and a desired signal.

concepts.name: autocorrelation
concepts.definition: Measures similarity between a signal and a delayed copy of itself versus lag, revealing periodicities and hidden patterns obscured by noise.

concepts.name: discrete_fourier_transform
concepts.definition: Converts a finite sampled sequence into discrete frequency components giving amplitude and phase, the core analysis tool of digital signal processing.

concepts.name: finite_impulse_response_filter
concepts.definition: Digital filter whose impulse response settles to zero in finite time, computing output as a weighted moving average of inputs; always stable.

concepts.name: matched_filter
concepts.definition: Linear filter that correlates input with a time-reversed template of a known signal to maximize SNR for detecting it in additive noise.

concepts.name: nyquist_sampling
concepts.definition: Theorem stating a band-limited signal is perfectly reconstructable from samples taken at least twice its highest frequency, avoiding aliasing.

concepts.name: quantization
concepts.definition: Maps a continuous range of signal values onto a finite set of discrete levels during analog-to-digital conversion, introducing quantization error.

concepts.name: spectrogram
concepts.definition: Squared-magnitude of the short-time Fourier transform, showing how a non-stationary signal's frequency content evolves over time.

concepts.name: wavelet_transform
concepts.definition: Decomposes a signal onto scaled and translated wavelet basis functions, giving joint time-frequency localization across multiple resolutions.

concepts.name: anomie
concepts.definition: Durkheim's concept of a societal state of normlessness, where weak or unclear norms break down moral regulation and guidance for individuals.

concepts.name: collective_action
concepts.definition: Coordinated effort by individuals or groups acting in unison to pursue a shared goal that cannot be achieved through individual action alone.

concepts.name: diffusion_of_innovations
concepts.definition: Rogers' theory of how new ideas and technologies spread through a social system over time via communication channels and adopter categories.

concepts.name: homophily
concepts.definition: The tendency of individuals to associate and bond with others similar to them, shaping the structure of social networks.

concepts.name: moral_panic
concepts.definition: Cohen's concept of disproportionate, widespread public fear that a condition, group, or person threatens societal values, amplified via media.

concepts.name: social_capital
concepts.definition: The networks of relationships, shared norms, trust, and reciprocity that let individuals and groups act effectively toward common goals.

concepts.name: social_mobility
concepts.definition: The movement of individuals or groups up or down a social hierarchy, measured by changes in income, education, or occupation across time or generations.

concepts.name: social_stratification
concepts.definition: A society's hierarchical ranking of people into groups with unequal access to wealth, power, and prestige based on socioeconomic factors.

concepts.name: strength_of_weak_ties
concepts.definition: Granovetter's finding that distant acquaintances (weak ties) bridge social groups and carry novel information better than close strong ties.

concepts.name: bayesian_inference
concepts.definition: Statistical inference that uses Bayes' theorem to update a prior probability of a hypothesis into a posterior as new data is observed.

concepts.name: bootstrap_resampling
concepts.definition: Resampling method that repeatedly draws samples with replacement from data to estimate standard errors, confidence intervals, and bias.

concepts.name: central_limit_theorem
concepts.definition: Theorem stating that the distribution of sample means approaches a normal distribution as sample size grows, regardless of the population distribution.

concepts.name: cross_validation
concepts.definition: Model validation technique that partitions data into folds to estimate how a fitted model generalizes to independent data and guard against overfitting.

concepts.name: expectation_maximization
concepts.definition: Iterative algorithm finding maximum-likelihood parameter estimates in models with latent variables by alternating expectation and maximization steps.

concepts.name: hypothesis_testing
concepts.definition: Inference method deciding whether sample data provide enough evidence to reject a null hypothesis using a test statistic and p-value.

concepts.name: kernel_density_estimation
concepts.definition: Non-parametric method estimating a probability density by placing a smoothing kernel on each data point and summing them.

concepts.name: markov_chain_monte_carlo
concepts.definition: Class of algorithms that sample from a probability distribution by building a Markov chain whose equilibrium distribution is the target.

concepts.name: maximum_likelihood_estimation
concepts.definition: Method of estimating model parameters by maximizing the likelihood that the assumed distribution produced the observed data.

concepts.name: principal_component_analysis
concepts.definition: Technique that transforms variables into uncorrelated principal components maximizing variance, reducing dimensionality with minimal information loss.
